pool.text: In a survey of students in Year 11 Group #1, \(|A| = 18\) study French, \(|B| = 15\) study Spanish, \(|A \cap B| = 5\) study both languages, and \(4\) study neither. Find the total number of students \(|\mathcal{E}|\).
pool.sol: By inclusion-exclusion, \(|A \cup B| = 18 + 15 - 5 = 28\). Adding the \(4\) outside \(A \cup B\) gives \(|\mathcal{E}| = 32\).
hints: Compute \(|A \cup B| = |A| + |B| - |A \cap B|\) so the overlap \(5\) is not double-counted.
Add the \(4\) students who belong to \((A \cup B)'\).
Combine \(28 + 4\) to obtain \(|\mathcal{E}|\).

pool.text: A rectangle has length \(13\text{ cm}\) and width \(9\text{ cm}\), each measured correct to the nearest centimetre. Calculate the upper bound of the area of the rectangle.

pool.text: A rectangle has length \(55\text{ cm}\) and width \(15\text{ cm}\), each measured correct to the nearest centimetre. Calculate the upper bound of the area of the rectangle.
pool.sol: Correct to the nearest \(1\text{ cm}\), the upper bounds are \(55.5\text{ cm}\) and \(15.5\text{ cm}\). Thus \(A_{\max} = 55.5 \times 15.5 = 860.25\text{ cm}^2\).

Multiply the two upper bounds to obtain the upper bound of the area.

pool.text: By completing the square for \(y = x^2 - 4x - 1\) (Case #1), find the coordinates of the turning point of the curve.
pool.sol: Completing the square gives \(y = (x - 2)^2 - 5\), which attains its minimum at \(x = 2\) with \(y = -5\), giving turning point \((2, -5)\).
hints: Factor \(1\) out of the \(x^2\) and \(x\) terms first.
Complete the square inside the bracket using half the coefficient of \(x\).
Read off the vertex \((h, k)\) from \(a(x - h)^2 + k\).

hints: Factor \(2\) out of the \(x^2\) and \(x\) terms first.
Complete the square inside the bracket using half the coefficient of \(x\).
Read off the vertex \((h, k)\) from \(a(x - h)^2 + k\).

pool.text: The accompanying figure illustrates a harmonic trace configuration (EDEXCEL-G7230); using it, compute the hypotenuse length \(AB\) from the side lengths labeled on right triangle \(ABC\).
pool.sol: By the Pythagorean theorem using legs \(12\) and \(16\) shown, \(AB = \sqrt{12^2 + 16^2} = 20\).
hints: Read the two numerical side lengths directly from the diagram; check which side is opposite the right angle.
Apply the Pythagorean identity a^2 + b^2 = c^2 with c as the hypotenuse opposite angle C.

pool.text: The accompanying figure illustrates a field geometry configuration (EDEXCEL-G8937); using it with parallel lines \(l \parallel m\). Using the co-interior angle labels shown, determine \(x\).
pool.sol: Co-interior angles on parallel lines are supplementary: \(66 + (2x ) = 180 \implies 2x = 114 \implies x = 57\).
hints: Same-side interior (co-interior) angles between parallel lines sum to 180 degrees.
Set up the linear equation adding the acute angle label and the algebraic obtuse label to 180.
Isolate x carefully after subtracting known constants.

pool.text: From the graphical features displayed in the acoustic chamber figure (EDEXCEL-G8984), find the exact area of the central sector using the radius and angle marked on the circle.
pool.sol: From the diagram, \(r = 8\) and central angle \(\theta = 180^\circ\), so sector area \(= \frac{180}{360}\pi(8)^2 = 32\pi\).
hints: Read both the radius r and central angle in degrees directly from the circle diagram.
Multiply full circle area pi*r^2 by the fraction (theta / 360).
Simplify the resulting coefficient of pi.

pool.text: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining \(A(6, 10)\) and \(B(8, 16)\) (Segment #53).
pool.sol: Midpoint \(M = (7, 13)\) and gradient \(m_{AB} = \frac{6}{2} = 3\). The perpendicular gradient is \(m_\perp = -\frac{1}{3}\), giving \(y - 13 = -\frac{1}{3}(x - 7)\), which simplifies to \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{46}{3}\).
hints: Calculate the midpoint \(M\) of \(A(6, 10)\) and \(B(8, 16)\).
Find the gradient \(m_{AB}\) and take its negative reciprocal \(m_\perp = -1 / m_{AB}\).
Substitute \(M\) and \(m_\perp\) into \(y - y_M = m_\perp(x - x_M)\) and rearrange into \(y = mx + c\) form.

pool.text: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining \(A(2, 8)\) and \(B(6, 16)\) (Segment #58).
pool.sol: Midpoint \(M = (4, 12)\) and gradient \(m_{AB} = \frac{8}{4} = 2\). The perpendicular gradient is \(m_\perp = -\frac{1}{2}\), giving \(y - 12 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)\), which simplifies to \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 14\).
hints: Calculate the midpoint \(M\) of \(A(2, 8)\) and \(B(6, 16)\).
Find the gradient \(m_{AB}\) and take its negative reciprocal \(m_\perp = -1 / m_{AB}\).
Substitute \(M\) and \(m_\perp\) into \(y - y_M = m_\perp(x - x_M)\) and rearrange into \(y = mx + c\) form.

pool.sol_ar: نقطة المنتصف \(M = (4, 4)\) و الميل \(m_{AB} = \frac{8}{4} = 2\). العمودي الميل يساوي \(m_\perp = -\frac{1}{2}\)، مما يعطي \(y - 4 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)\)، التي يتبسّط إلى \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 6\).
hints_ar: احسب نقطة المنتصف \(M\) من \(A(2, 0)\) و \(B(6, 8)\).
أوجد الميل \(m_{AB}\) و خذ له سالب مقلوب \(m_\perp = -1 / m_{AB}\).
عوّض \(M\) و \(m_\perp\) إلى \(y - y_M = m_\perp(x - x_M)\) و أعد ترتيب إلى \(y = mx + c\) الصيغة.

pool.text: In \(\triangle ABC\) (#2), \(AB = 6\text{ cm}\), \(AC = 8\text{ cm}\), and \(\angle BAC = 60^\circ\). Using the Cosine Rule, find the exact length of \(BC\).
pool.sol: By the Cosine Rule, \(BC^2 = 6^2 + 8^2 - 2(6)(8)\cos 60^\circ = 36 + 64 - 48 = 52\), so \(BC = \sqrt{52}\text{ cm}\).
hints: Apply \(BC^2 = AB^2 + AC^2 - 2(AB)(AC)\cos(\angle BAC)\).
Use \(\cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\) so \(2(AB)(AC)\cos 60^\circ = AB \cdot AC\).
Evaluate \(6^2 + 8^2 - (6)(8)\) and take the positive square root.
pool.educational_aim: 3D Trigonometry, Sine/Cosine Rules & Vector Proofs: apply applying triangle similarity, right-triangle trigonometry, and trigonometric laws across multi-step.

hints: Compute consecutive first differences q(1)-q(0), q(2)-q(1), and q(3)-q(2).

Add the constant second difference to the last first difference to advance from x = 3 to x = 4.

pool.text: Find the coordinates of the local minimum stationary point on the curve \(y = 2x^3 - 24x + 3\) for \(x > 0\) (Curve #2).
pool.sol: Differentiating gives \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 6x^2 - 24 = 0 \implies x^2 = 4\). For \(x > 0\), \(x = 2\) with \(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 24 > 0\), and \(y(2) = -29\).
hints: Differentiate \(y\) with respect to \(x\) using the power rule.

Substitute \(x\) back into the original cubic equation to find the \(y\)-coordinate.

hints_ar: ابدأ بالعمود \(x = 2\) واقرأ قيمة \(g(2)\) من الصف الأخير.
استخدم الناتج كمدخل في صف \(x\) العلوي لإيجاد \(f(g(2))\) .
أضف \(3\) إلى الناتج النهائي وتحقق من دقة الصفوف.

figure.caption: Selected values of functions f and g (calorimetry, EDEXCEL-15709)

pool.text: A benchmark navigation log (EDEXCEL-15778) provides the entries shown in the table; determine \(3\,h^{-1}(11)\) for the invertible function \(h\).
pool.sol: Because \(h(5) = 11\), we have \(h^{-1}(11) = 5\). Multiplying by \(3\) gives \(15\).
hints: To evaluate h^-1(11), scan the h(x) row rather than the x row to locate 11.
Match the column containing h(x) = 11 back up to its input x.
Multiply that inverse input by 3 to complete the calculation.
pool.educational_aim: Differentiation, Turning Points & Kinematics: apply modeling and solving linear or nonlinear inequalities across multi-step problems (edx calculus kinematics.
pool.text_ar: يقدّم سجل الملاحة (EDEXCEL-15778) القياسات الموضحة في الجدول: لإيجاد قيمة \(3\,h^{-1}(11)\) للدالة العكسية \(h\) .
pool.sol_ar: بما أن \(h(5) = 11\) فإن \(h^{-1}(11) = 5\) ، وبضربها في \(3\) يكون الناتج \(15\) .
hints_ar: ابحث عن العدد \(11\) في صف \(h(x)\) وليس في صف \(x\) .
اقرأ قيمة \(x\) المقابلة في العمود نفسه لتحديد الدالة العكسية.
اضرب قيمة \(x\) المستخرجة في المعامل \(3\) .

pool.text: The table summarizes measurements from a circuit trial evaluation (EDEXCEL-15847); using these entries, tracking Euler's method with constant step \(h = 1\). Determine the missing approximation \(y_2\).
hints: Use Euler recurrence y_{n+1} = y_n + h * (dy/dx at x_n).
Read y1 and the slope (dy/dx) from step n = 1, not step n = 0.

pool.educational_aim: Differentiation, Turning Points & Kinematics: apply modeling and solving linear or nonlinear inequalities across multi-step problems (edx calculus kinematics.
pool.text_ar: يلخّص الجدول قياسات مسجّلة من تجربة تجربة الدائرة (EDEXCEL-15847). بالاعتماد على القيم المعطاة، لتتبع طريقة أويلر بخطوة \(h = 1\) . أوجد القيمة التقريبية المفقودة \(y_2\) .
pool.sol_ar: من صف الخطوة الأولى نجد \(y_2 = 6 + 1 \times 2 = 8\) .
hints_ar: استخدم علاقة أويلر باستخدام قيم الصف السابق \(n = 1\) .

pool.text: Find the coordinates of the local minimum stationary point on the curve \(y = 4x^3 - 48x + 15\) for \(x > 0\) (Curve #104).
pool.sol: Differentiating gives \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 12x^2 - 48 = 0 \implies x^2 = 4\). For \(x > 0\), \(x = 2\) with \(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 48 > 0\), and \(y(2) = -49\).

Set \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\) and select the positive stationary value \(x > 0\).
Substitute \(x\) back into the original cubic equation to find the \(y\)-coordinate.
